charts.title: Option verbosity vs shared wording
charts.description: Longer answer choices tend to reuse more vocabulary across the four options. That can help text models without identifying a reliable answer position.

charts.title: Prompt overlap vs shared option wording
charts.description: Boards whose options echo the question also tend to repeat wording between options, a plausible source of lexical rather than sequence signal.

charts.title: Numeric-option count vs option length
charts.description: Boards with more numeric choices use shorter answer text. This separates a format effect from any supposed preferred answer letter.

charts.title: Option scale vs length imbalance
charts.description: Longer answer sets naturally have a wider length range, so raw longest-answer heuristics need to account for the board's overall text scale.

charts.title: Option verbosity vs prompt overlap
charts.description: Verbose choices have more opportunities to reuse prompt words. The relationship is real but does not by itself reveal which option is correct.

charts.title: Question position vs option verbosity
charts.description: Later ladder positions use slightly longer options. The weak slope is useful context for difficulty features, not a standalone prediction rule.
